question.text: Mrs. Patel sets up an SWP of Rs. 25,000 per month from an equity fund. She holds 5,000 units at a current NAV of Rs. 120. How many units will be redeemed in the first month, and how many units will remain?

answer.text: 208.33 units redeemed, 5,000 units remaining (new units are added)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under an SWP, the fixed withdrawal amount is divided by the prevailing NAV to determine the units redeemed. Units redeemed = Rs. 25,000 / Rs. 120 = 208.33 units. Remaining units = 5,000 - 208.33 = 4,791.67 units. The Trap: SWP redeems UNITS, not the NAV. The number of units redeemed varies each month depending on the NAV at the time of withdrawal. If NAV rises, fewer units are redeemed for the same Rs. 25,000; if NAV falls, more units are redeemed. Note: SWP redemptions reduce the unit-holding over time and may attract applicable exit loads and taxes.
